title: xproxy configuration
description: One YAML document read by xproxy. Unknown keys are errors; omitted values take the documented defaults. See docs/CONFIG.md and xproxy.yaml(5).

acme.description: ACME configures automatic certificates for listeners with tls.acme.

api_inventory.description: APIInventory records the endpoints the proxy serves and reports shadow, zombie and superseded APIs.

bans.description: Bans enables the ban list when present.

cache.description: Cache sizes the in-memory response cache used by routes[].cache.

capture.description: Capture writes the exchanges the proxy handled as pcapng files, for the flows its rules select.

challenge.description: Challenge configures the browser challenge used by routes with a challenge block.

cluster.description: Cluster enables sharing of rate limit consumption and bans between proxies when present.

compression.description: Compression enables gzip of eligible responses on every route (routes[].compress overrides per route).

degradation.description: Degradation serves a suspect client slowly rather than refusing it outright.

filters.description: Filters are middleware instances of registered kinds (see docs/EXTENDING.md) that routes attach by name.

fleet.description: Fleet makes this node fetch its configuration bundle from a fleet controller and report its status there (xproxy-fleet).

geoip.description: GeoIP names the country database used by routes[].geo and by rate limits keyed on country.

handshake.description: Handshake refuses clients before the TLS handshake completes.

honeytokens.description: Honeytokens are planted credentials. A request presenting one has read something it should not have.

icap.description: ICAP configures external scanning services referenced by routes.

includes.description: Includes are absolute glob patterns of fragment files whose upstreams, routes, rate_limits and filters are appended to this document, in lexical order of path. Fragments may contain nothing else; names must not repeat. Read at every load and reload.

ingress.description: Ingress turns Kubernetes Ingress resources into routes, upstreams and certificates (ingress controller mode).

jwt.description: JWT configures token providers referenced by routes.

maintenance.description: Maintenance serves a 503 to everyone but an allowlist while it is on. The section sets the policy and the boot state; the state is toggled at runtime (POST /v1/maintenance, xproxyctl maintenance).

metrics.description: Metrics tunes exposition and the time series buffer.

sandbox.description: Sandbox configures the in-process hardening applied once the listeners are bound: Landlock file system rules, a seccomp system call filter, capability dropping and debugger denial on Linux; debugger denial and core dump suppression on macOS. On by default.

security_txt.description: SecurityTxt serves a virtual security.txt (RFC 9116) for the hosts each entry names, before routing.

shedding.description: Shedding enables adaptive load shedding by priority class when present.

tracing.description: Tracing gives requests a W3C trace context and exports spans.

trusted_proxies.description: TrustedProxies lists CIDRs whose X-Forwarded-For / Forwarded headers are trusted for client IP derivation. Empty means never trust such headers.

version.description: Version is the schema version. Must equal CurrentVersion.

virtual_patches.description: VirtualPatches block known vulnerabilities by request shape.

waf.description: WAF enables the web application firewall when present.

ACME.description: ACME configures the certificate authority account (RFC 8555; AMR-029).

accept_terms.description: AcceptTerms must be true; the CA's terms are agreed on registration.

ca_file.description: CAFile pins the CA of the directory server (private CAs, tests).

challenge.description: Challenge is http-01 (needs a plaintext listener on port 80) or tls-alpn-01 (needs the TLS listener on port 443). Default http-01.

check_interval.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

directory.description: Directory is the CA's directory URL.

renew_before.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

state_dir.description: StateDir holds the account key and issued certificates. Default /var/lib/xproxy/acme.

ACMEGroup.description: ACMEGroup is one automatically managed certificate.

APIInventory.description: APIInventory discovers the API surface from traffic: every proxied request is attributed to a host, method and path template, with counts, credentials seen, media types and the version in the path. Routes with an openapi filter contribute their documented operations, which makes shadow endpoints (traffic outside the description) and zombies (documented operations without traffic) visible.

enabled.description: Enabled defaults to true when the section is present.

hosts.description: Hosts and Routes narrow the inventory to these host patterns and route names. Default: every proxied route.

save_interval.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

state_file.description: StateFile keeps the inventory across restarts. Optional.

zombie_after.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

Affinity.description: Affinity is signed cookie session affinity.

secret_file.description: SecretFile holds the HMAC key. Generated at first start when absent and the directory is writable.

ttl.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

BanTrigger.description: BanTrigger bans a client after Threshold denies within Window.

aggregate.description: Aggregate is what the trigger counts and bans: address (default), net (the client network of NetV4 or NetV6 bits, for attacks spread over one allocation) or ja4 (the TLS client fingerprint, for attacks spread over many networks from one tool).

duration.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

escalation.description: Escalation multiplies the duration for every repeat ban of the same address. Default 2. MaxDuration caps it, default 24h.

max_duration.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

min_sources.description: MinSources is how many distinct client addresses must contribute to the window before a net or ja4 aggregate bans, so one noisy host does not ban its neighbours. Default 1.

net_v4.description: NetV4 and NetV6 are the prefix lengths of aggregate net. Default 24 and 48.

reasons.description: Reasons restricts which deny reasons count (acl, rate_limit, waf, body_size, uri_length, bad_host, no_route, websocket, concurrency). Empty counts every deny.

window.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

Bans.description: Bans configures the ban list: addresses that are refused outright for a period after repeated security denies or by operator action.

action.description: Action is drop (close connections at accept and answer 403 when the client is derived from a trusted proxy) or reject (403 only). Default drop.

exempt_cidrs.description: ExemptCIDRs are never banned (monitoring, office ranges).

max_entries.description: MaxEntries bounds the number of banned addresses. Default 100000.

state_file.description: StateFile persists bans across restarts (bbolt). Empty keeps them in memory only.

triggers.description: Triggers turn repeated denies into bans.

CRS.description: CRS tunes the Core Rule Set.

dir.description: Dir loads the rule set from a directory laid out like a CRS release (crs-setup.conf or crs-setup.conf.example, rules/*.conf and the data files) instead of the copy embedded in the binary, so that rules can be updated with a reload. Default: embedded.

inbound_threshold.description: InboundThreshold is the anomaly score at which a request is blocked. Default 5 (one critical rule).

outbound_threshold.description: OutboundThreshold is the anomaly score at which a response is blocked. Default 4.

plugins.description: Plugins names the plugins under PluginsDir to load. Default: every plugin found.

plugins_dir.description: PluginsDir holds CRS plugins, each a directory or a set of files named <plugin>-config.conf, <plugin>-before.conf and <plugin>-after.conf. Config and before files load before the CRS rules, after files after them.

CT.description: CT is the Certificate Transparency policy for file certificates.

enforce.description: Enforce fails the load or reload of a certificate below Require instead of logging it.

log_list_file.description: LogListFile is a log list in Google's JSON format with the logs' keys; with it SCT signatures are verified.

require.description: Require is the number of embedded SCTs a certificate must carry (verified ones when LogListFile is set). 0 only reports.

Cache.description: Cache bounds the response cache. Default 64 MiB total, 1 MiB per object.

Canary.description: Canary routes selected requests to the pool's canary endpoints: those carrying Header or Cookie (with one of Values when listed) and a Percent share of the rest. Other requests avoid the canaries. Each side falls back to the other when its endpoints are all unavailable unless Fallback is false.

Captcha.description: Captcha configures a hosted CAPTCHA provider for the challenge.

hostnames.description: Hostnames the provider may report the token was solved on. Empty checks the token against the host the challenge page was served on, so a token solved for another site is refused. HostnameCheck off disables the check for providers that do not return a hostname.

min_score.description: MinScore refuses tokens the provider scores below it (reCAPTCHA v3 and Enterprise return one). Default 0 (not checked).

mode.description: Mode is escalation (default: the widget only for verdicts that ask for a CAPTCHA) or always (every challenge page).

provider.description: Provider is turnstile, hcaptcha or recaptcha.

secret_file.description: SecretFile holds the provider's secret key (one line).

site_key.description: SiteKey is the public key rendered into the widget.

timeout.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

verify_url.description: VerifyURL overrides the provider's siteverify endpoint (tests, enterprise endpoints).

Capture.description: Capture writes the exchanges the proxy handled as pcapng files that Wireshark and tshark read. The proxy terminates TLS, so a capture taken on the wire in front of it is ciphertext and one taken behind it has lost the client; this is the proxy's own view of the decrypted exchange, synthesised into a TCP conversation so a dissector reads it as HTTP. A capture file holds request and response bytes in the clear: cookies, bearer tokens, personal data, whatever the application carries. It is written 0600 into a directory the operator names, nothing else is ever put there, and `redact` blanks the header values that should not be in it at all. Treat the directory as you would treat the access log with redaction turned off.

bodies.description: Bodies captures request and response bodies as well as the heads. Default false: the heads answer most questions and carry far less of what should not be on disk.

directory.description: Directory holds the files. Absolute, and owned by the proxy user.

enabled.description: Enabled builds the subsystem. Without it nothing is recorded and the runtime switch has nothing to turn on.

file_prefix.description: FilePrefix begins each file name; the rest is the time it was opened. Default "xproxy".

max_body_bytes.description: MaxBodyBytes bounds each captured body; the rest is left out and the frame is marked truncated. Default 65536.

max_duration.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

max_file_bytes.description: MaxFileBytes rotates to a new file past this size. Default 64 MiB.

max_files.description: MaxFiles keeps this many files, removing the oldest. Default 4.

redact.description: Redact blanks these request and response header values in the captured bytes. Default: the authorization, cookie and API key headers.

rules.description: Rules select which exchanges are written. No rules means every exchange, which is what a section with only a directory means.

snap_len.description: SnapLen is the largest frame written. Default 262144.

start_active.description: StartActive begins recording at start-up. Default false: the usual shape is a configuration that is ready and a switch an operator throws for one reproduction.

CaptureRule.description: CaptureRule selects exchanges. Every selector it names must hold, and a rule that names none matches everything; the first rule that matches decides. Selectors on the answer (statuses, reasons, denied) are only known once the exchange is over, so a rule using them captures the whole exchange retrospectively.

client_cidrs.description: ClientCIDRs restrict the rule to these client networks.

denied.description: Denied selects every refusal, whatever the reason.

hosts.description: Hosts are exact names or "*.example.com" patterns.

max_flows.description: MaxFlows bounds how many exchanges this rule ever writes, so a rule left on cannot fill a disk. 0 is unbounded.

name.description: Name identifies the rule in the status view.

paths.description: Paths are prefixes of the routing path.

percent.description: Percent samples the exchanges this rule would take. Default 100.

reasons.description: Reasons are deny reasons ("waf", "rate_limit", ...), matched against the reason and against the reason with its detail.

statuses.description: Statuses are response statuses, or classes 1 to 5.

Certificate.description: Certificate references a PEM certificate chain and private key on disk.

Challenge.description: Challenge configures the browser proof-of-work challenge (AMR-023).

title.description: Title is the heading shown on the page.

bind_ip.description: BindIP ties the cookie to the client address. Default true.

bind_ja4.description: BindJA4 ties the cookie to the client's JA4 TLS fingerprint (token binding): a cookie earned by one TLS client is refused when replayed by another, even from the same address. Off by default; TLS only.

captcha.description: Captcha adds a hosted CAPTCHA tier: verdicts that ask for one (an account_guard captcha step) show the provider's widget instead of the proof of work; with mode always every challenge page does.

cookie_scope.description: CookieScope is "shared" (default) or "host". A pass cookie is bound to the client address and its TLS fingerprint; with "host" it is bound to the host that served the challenge as well, so a client cannot earn a cheap pass on one host and spend it on another that asks for more work. Use "host" when hosts behind one proxy differ in difficulty or tier; leave it "shared" when a pass is meant to cover a site's several names, since "host" makes every outstanding cookie stop working once.

device.description: Device includes a device identifier, computed by the challenge script from stable browser properties, in the cookie; it becomes the device attribute, Info.DeviceID for filters and the device rate limit key. Default true.

difficulty.description: Difficulty is the number of leading zero bits required. Default 16 (about 65 000 hashes, well under a second in a browser).

secret_file.description: SecretFile persists the HMAC key so cookies survive restarts.

ttl.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

CircuitBreaker.description: CircuitBreaker is a pool wide breaker: closed counts consecutive failures (connection errors, timeouts, 503 and retry_on statuses), open refuses requests with 503 for OpenFor (times the number of reopens, at most ten), half open lets HalfOpenRequests trials through.

open_for.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

Cluster.description: Cluster configures peer to peer sharing over mutual TLS (AMR-009).

exact_timeout.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

gossip_interval.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

listen.description: Listen is the address of the cluster listener (TCP, mTLS). Bind it to an internal interface.

node_id.description: NodeID identifies this node to peers. Default: host name.

peer_stale.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

peers.description: Peers are the cluster addresses of the other nodes.

share_rate_limits.description: ShareRateLimits, ShareBans and ShareEvents select what is exchanged. All default to true. Events are honeypot marks and revoked OIDC sessions; nodes older than 1.3 close a connection that carries them.

ClusterTLS.description: ClusterTLS holds the node certificate and the cluster CA. Every peer must present a certificate from this CA; there is no other authentication.

allowed_names.description: AllowedNames optionally restricts peers to these certificate common names or DNS SANs.

bind_node_id.description: BindNodeID requires a peer's announced node_id to be a name its certificate carries. Default true. The id is not a label: key ownership for exact rate limits is a rendezvous hash over node ids, so a peer free to choose its id chooses which keys it decides for every node. Set it false only for an existing cluster whose certificate names and node ids differ, and fix the certificates: a cluster certificate is full trust within the cluster, and the id is the only thing that distinguishes one holder of one from another. The id is not a label: key ownership for exact rate limits is a rendezvous hash over node ids, and bans and marks are attributed to them, so a peer that chooses its own id chooses which keys it decides and whose name appears in the audit trail. Set it false only for an existing cluster whose certificate names differ from its node ids, and fix the certificates.

Compression.description: Compression is the gzip policy for responses the proxy writes: proxied, cached, static and respond bodies alike. Responses the upstream already encoded, ranges, `no-transform` and unlisted media types pass through.

compress_authenticated.description: CompressAuthenticated compresses a response to a request that carried Authorization or Cookie. Default false. Compressing a response that mixes a secret with attacker-chosen text leaks the secret through the compressed length, one character at a time (BREACH). The condition is a request the attacker can make the browser send with the victim's credentials, which is exactly a request carrying a cookie. Turn it on per route where the response holds no secret, or where the application already masks its tokens.

enabled.description: Enabled defaults to true when the section is present.

encodings.description: Encodings lists the content encodings offered, in the order the proxy prefers them when a client accepts several with equal quality: br (Brotli), zstd and gzip. Default [br, zstd, gzip].

level.description: Level is the gzip level 1 (fastest) to 9 (smallest). Default 5.

min_bytes.description: MinBytes is the smallest body compressed when its length is known or once that much has been buffered. Default 1024.

types.description: Types lists the media types compressed (without parameters). Default: the common text, script, style, JSON, XML, SVG and wasm types.

DNSCache.description: DNSCache bounds the cache of a dns listener.

max_ttl.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

min_ttl.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

negative_ttl.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

DNSDesignated.description: DNSDesignated is one encrypted endpoint advertised by discovery.

doh_path.description: DoHPath is the URI template for a doh endpoint. Default /dns-query{?dns}.

ipv4.description: IPv4 and IPv6 are address hints, so a client need not resolve the name it was just handed.

name.description: Name is the certificate name clients verify. It must be a name the endpoint's certificate covers, or the upgrade fails closed.

port.description: Port the endpoint listens on. Default 853 for dot and doq, 443 for doh.

transport.description: Transport is dot, doh or doq.

ttl.description: TTL of the discovery records. Default 300.

DNSListener.description: DNSListener is a forwarding DNS proxy on the listener address over UDP and TCP: a bounded cache, a block policy and forwarding to upstream resolvers with fresh transaction ids and source ports. The policy, upstreams and cache bounds reload; the address needs a restart.

allow_clients.description: AllowClients restricts clients to these CIDRs (others get REFUSED). Empty allows any client.

block.description: Block lists names: a bare name blocks it and its subdomains, *.suffix only subdomains, =name only that name.

block_action.description: BlockAction is nxdomain (default), refuse or sinkhole.

block_file.description: BlockFile adds names from a file (one per line, hosts file lines accepted), read at load and reload.

discovery.description: Discovery advertises this resolver's encrypted endpoints at _dns.resolver.arpa (RFC 9462), so a client handed this address by DHCP can upgrade itself from plaintext DNS.

dnssec.description: DNSSEC validates upstream answers against a trust anchor.

doh_path.description: DoHPath is the DNS over HTTPS path served on an encrypted dns listener (one with tls). Default /dns-query.

doq.description: DoQ also serves DNS over QUIC (RFC 9250) on this listener's address over UDP. Needs tls; the certificate is shared with DoT and DoH, since they are the same service.

log_queries.description: LogQueries writes one dns line per query to the access log. Default false (query logs are personal data).

max_in_flight.description: MaxInFlight bounds queries being handled. Default 1024.

rate_limit.description: RateLimit bounds queries per client; over it queries are dropped.

records.description: Records are SVCB and HTTPS records this resolver answers itself, most usefully the ECH configuration of a name this proxy terminates.

sinkhole_ipv4.description: SinkholeIPv4 and SinkholeIPv6 answer A and AAAA for blocked names with block_action sinkhole. Default 0.0.0.0 and ::.

timeout.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

upstream_ca_file.description: UpstreamCAFile pins the CA of tls:// and https:// upstreams. Default: system pool.

upstreams.description: Upstreams are resolvers tried in turn: host:port (UDP with TCP fallback), tls://host:port (DNS over TLS) or https://host/path (DNS over HTTPS). Required.

DNSRateLimit.description: DNSRateLimit is a per client token bucket.

DNSRecord.description: DNSRecord is one locally served SVCB or HTTPS record.

name.description: Name the record is published for.

params.description: Params are service parameters in presentation form: {alpn: "h2,h3", port: "443", ech: "AEr+DQ...", ipv4hint: "..."}.

priority.description: Priority 0 makes it an alias record, which takes no parameters.

target.description: Target is the endpoint name; "." means the owner name itself.

DNSSEC.description: DNSSEC configures validation on a dns listener: answers are fetched with the DO bit, signatures and denial proofs are checked up to a trust anchor, secure answers carry AD, bogus answers become SERVFAIL (unless the client set CD), insecure answers pass without AD.

enabled.description: Enabled defaults to true when the section is present.

max_lookups.description: MaxLookups bounds DNSKEY and DS queries per answer. Default 48.

trust_anchors.description: TrustAnchors are DS records ("zone keytag algorithm digesttype digest"); the IANA root keys are built in.

trust_anchors_file.description: TrustAnchorsFile adds DS lines from a file (comments with #).

Deceive.description: Deceive answers a client the proxy no longer trusts with something plausible instead of with the origin's answer — or with a refusal. A refusal is information. A scanner that gets 403 knows the request it sent was the interesting one, and varies it until something is not refused; the refusal is the oracle that tells it when it has found the way through. An answer that looks ordinary gives it nothing to steer by: the crawl completes, the data is wrong, and the request that would have worked looks exactly like the one that did not. It is a deliberately sharp tool, and the rules follow from that: - It applies only to clients the proxy already has a reason to distrust — a honeypot or honeytoken mark, a bot score, a named network. A route with no condition is refused at validation, because a deceive that admits everyone is an outage that looks like a feature. - The write never reaches the origin. That is the point for a POST, and it means a false positive loses a client's data, so the conditions are worth being sure of. - It is loud on the inside. The access log line carries deceived: <route>, a security event records it, and the counter and metric are separate from every other refusal, so nobody debugs a "working" endpoint for a week.

bot_score_at.description: BotScoreAt admits a request a bot_score filter scored at or above this. 0 does not look at the score.

content_type.description: ContentType of Body and BodyFile. Default text/html; a decoy brings its own.

decoy.description: Decoy names a built-in decoy body (see routes[].honeypot), Body is a literal one and BodyFile is read from disk at load and reload. Exactly one is required.

mark.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

marked.description: Marked admits a client a honeypot route or a honeytoken marked.

methods.description: Methods narrows the deception to these methods; empty is all of them.

status.description: Status answers the deceived request. Default 200: the whole point is an answer that does not look like a refusal.

Degradation.description: Degradation serves a suspect client slowly instead of refusing it. The proxy's other answers are binary: served, or refused. For a client that has done something wrong but not enough to ban — touched a decoy, scored badly, arrived from a range with a history — both are wrong. Serving it in full funds the next request. Refusing it tells it exactly which request to change, and hands a scanner a clean signal to tune against. A degraded client is served, correctly, slowly. There is nothing to tune against and nothing to report as broken, and a crawl that cost the scanner nothing now costs it the thing it has least of. Levels are tried in order and the first that admits the request decides, so the narrowest goes first.

DegradeLevel.description: DegradeLevel is one rule: who is degraded, and by how much.

bot_score_at.description: BotScoreAt admits a request whose bot_score filter scored it at or above this. 0 does not look at the score.

bytes_per_second.description: BytesPerSecond shapes the response body. 0 does not shape.

client_cidrs.description: ClientCIDRs narrows the level to these client networks.

close.description: Close ends the connection after the response, so the client pays for a new one every time.

delay.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

marked.description: Marked admits a client a honeypot route or a honeytoken marked.

methods.description: Methods narrows it to these methods.

name.description: Name identifies the level in the access log, the metrics and the management view.

routes.description: Routes narrows it to these route names.

Discovery.description: Discovery resolves a pool's endpoints from DNS or an HTTP registry.

type.description: Type is dns (A and AAAA records of Name, each with Port), srv (SRV records of Name; targets and ports come from the records, the lowest priority group is used and record weights become endpoint weights) or http (Name is a URL polled on the interval; see Format).

canary.description: Canary marks discovered endpoints as canaries.

format.description: Format is the response shape for type http: list (default, a JSON array of {address|host,port, weight?, canary?}) or consul (the Consul /v1/health/service response; only passing instances are used and their Weights.Passing becomes the endpoint weight).

headers.description: Headers are extra request headers for type http, for example an authentication token (Consul: X-Consul-Token).

interval.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

name.description: Name is the DNS name to resolve (for srv the full _service._proto name), or, for type http, the registry URL to poll.

port.description: Port is the endpoint port for type dns, and the default port for type http when the registry omits one. Ignored for srv.

resolver.description: Resolver is an optional host:port of the DNS server to ask instead of the system resolver. DNS types only.

timeout.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

weight.description: Weight given to discovered endpoints (type dns and http list format entries without their own weight). Default 1.

ECH.description: ECH configures Encrypted Client Hello: the client encrypts the real ClientHello (SNI included) to a key published in DNS, and sends it inside an outer hello that names a shared public name.

keys.description: Keys are the configurations this listener can decrypt. Several are live at once during a rotation.

require.description: Require refuses a handshake that did not use ECH. It cuts off every client that has not got the key — including one whose DNS answer was stripped — so it is for a listener that exists only for ECH clients.

ECHKey.description: ECHKey is one ECH configuration and its private key.

config_file.description: ConfigFile holds the ECHConfig, raw or base64, as written by `xproxyctl ech keygen`.

key_file.description: KeyFile holds the X25519 private key, raw, base64 or hex. It must not be world readable.

retry.description: Retry offers this config to a client whose key was stale, which is how a rotation heals itself. Default true.

Endpoint.description: Endpoint is a single upstream address.

canary.description: Canary marks the endpoint as the pool's canary: it receives the requests the pool's canary policy selects and no others.

ErrorPages.description: ErrorPages replaces the plain status bodies the proxy writes (denials, upstream failures, unknown routes, static misses) with documents from a directory, chosen by exact status ("404"), class ("4xx", "5xx") or "default". Documents are read at load and may use ${status}, ${status_text}, ${request_id}, ${host}, ${path}, ${reason} and the other request variables; unknown ${...} sequences are kept as they are.

content_type.description: ContentType of the documents. Default text/html; charset=utf-8.

dir.description: Dir holds the documents; page values are file names inside it or absolute paths.

intercept_upstream.description: InterceptUpstream lists upstream response statuses whose bodies are replaced by the matching page (typically 502, 503, 504). Default none: upstream bodies pass through.

json.description: JSON answers clients whose Accept prefers application/json with a small JSON document instead of the page. Default true.

kind.description: Kind is a registered filter kind (xproxyctl filters lists them).

options.description: Options are kind specific and validated by the kind at load.

stage.description: Stage places the filter relative to the built-in chain: before_auth (before JWT), after_auth (default; after JWT, before the WAF), after_waf (before ICAP) or after_scan (last).

Fleet.description: Fleet is the agent side of central configuration management: the node long polls the controller for a bundle whose digest differs from the applied one, writes the files under Dir, reloads and reports its status. Changing the section requires a restart.

apply.description: Apply false reports status and pending bundles without writing or reloading anything. Default true.

controller.description: Controller is the controller's base URL (https).

dir.description: Dir receives the bundle files; the configuration file must be Dir/xproxy.yaml (the -config path). Default: the directory of the configuration file.

interval.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

node_id.description: NodeID is the node's name at the controller; it must match the certificate name unless the controller runs with -any-name. Default cluster.node_id, else the host name.

tags.description: Tags are reported to the controller for grouping.

timeout.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

tls.description: TLS holds the node certificate, key and the fleet CA.

FleetTLS.description: FleetTLS is the agent's client certificate and the controller CA.

server_name.description: ServerName overrides the name verified in the controller's certificate. Default: the host of Controller.

ForwardAuth.description: ForwardAuth is the credential source of a forward listener.

realm.description: Realm is sent in Proxy-Authenticate. Default "proxy".

users_file.description: UsersFile holds name:hash lines from xproxyctl htpasswd. Re-read on reload.

ForwardListener.description: ForwardListener is an explicit forward proxy: clients send CONNECT host:port for tunnels (TLS stays end to end) or absolute http:// URIs for plain requests. Destinations are policy checked by name, resolved address and port; private and loopback addresses are refused unless allow_private is set, and the checked address is the one dialled.

allow.description: Allow restricts destinations to these names (exact or *.suffix), addresses or CIDRs. Empty allows any destination not denied.

allow_private.description: AllowPrivate permits loopback, link local, private and unique local destination addresses. Default false.

connect_timeout.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

deny.description: Deny refuses destinations matching these names, addresses or CIDRs. Deny wins over allow and is checked against the resolved addresses too.

idle_timeout.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

masque.description: Masque enables the MASQUE proxying protocols on this listener.

max_response_bytes.description: MaxResponseBytes bounds the body of a plain (non CONNECT) response relayed to the client. Default 64 MiB; 0 disables.

max_tunnels.description: MaxTunnels bounds open CONNECT tunnels on this listener. Default 10000.

ports.description: Ports destinations may be reached on (CONNECT and plain). Default [80, 443].

socks5.description: SOCKS5 also accepts SOCKS5 (RFC 1928) on this listener. The two protocols share the port: a greeting starts with the version byte and an HTTP request with a method, so one byte tells them apart. Destinations, ports, credentials, bans and logging are the same.

socks_udp.description: SOCKSUDP allows UDP ASSOCIATE, which is how DNS and QUIC travel through a SOCKS proxy. Each association is bound to the client address that opened it and dies with its control connection.

GeoIP.description: GeoIP configures the country database: a MaxMind DB file (GeoLite2 or GeoIP2 Country, or any MMDB with country.iso_code) or a CSV of "network,country" lines.

H3.description: H3 configures the QUIC listener of a TLS listener (AMR-024).

alt_svc_max_age.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

max_streams.description: MaxStreams bounds concurrent request streams per connection. Default 100.

validate_addresses.description: ValidateAddresses is always (every new client address must complete a Retry round trip before any state is allocated) or under_load (only when open connections exceed a quarter of max_connections). Default always.

webtransport.description: WebTransport accepts WebTransport sessions (extended CONNECT with HTTP/3 datagrams) on this endpoint; routes with webtransport relay them. Default false.

Handshake.description: Handshake decides who is refused before a TLS handshake completes. Every other control in this file answers a request: the handshake runs, a certificate is chosen, keys are agreed, the request is parsed, and then the proxy says no. For a client already known to be unwelcome that is a lot of asymmetric cryptography spent on saying no, and an answer — a status, a page, a header set — that tells a scanner something about what is in front of it. Refusing in the ClientHello is the cheapest possible no and the quietest: the connection fails to negotiate and there is nothing to fingerprint. It applies to every TLS listener, including HTTP/3, and to nothing else: a plain HTTP listener has no handshake to refuse in, and what arrives there is still refused the ordinary way.

deny_fingerprints.description: DenyFingerprints refuses these TLS fingerprints outright, whatever the ban list says. An entry is a JA4 or JA3 string, or one prefixed "ja4:" or "ja3:" to name which it is; a JA4 entry ending in "*" matches by prefix, which is how a family of clients is named without pinning every extension order.

log.description: Log records each refusal in the security log (reason "handshake"). Default true.

refuse_banned.description: RefuseBanned refuses a client whose address or TLS fingerprint is on the ban list. Default false: a ban that answers 403 is visible to the operator in the access log, and this makes the refusal invisible there, which is a deliberate trade.

HeaderMatch.description: HeaderMatch is one condition on a request header or cookie: exactly one of Exact, Prefix, Regex or Present. Header names are matched case insensitively and the first value is used; cookie names are exact.

exact.description: Exact requires the value to equal this string.

prefix.description: Prefix requires the value to start with this string.

present.description: Present true requires the header or cookie to exist with any value; false requires it to be absent.

regex.description: Regex is an RE2 pattern matched against the whole value.

when.description: When restricts the operations to requests for which the expression holds (docs/CONFIG.md, "Expressions"); empty applies them always.

HealthCheck.description: HealthCheck configures active health probing of an upstream.

type.description: Type is http (GET path, expected_status) or grpc (the standard grpc.health.v1 Check over HTTP/2, needs h2c or https). Default http.

body_contains.description: BodyContains requires the first 64 KiB of the probe response to contain this text (type http); BodyRegex an RE2 pattern to match anywhere in it. Both may be set; both must hold.

grpc_service.description: GRPCService is the service name asked in a grpc check. Default "" (the server as a whole).

interval.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

keep_alive.description: KeepAlive reuses pooled connections for probes. Off (the default) opens a fresh connection per probe, which verifies the whole connect path and holds no descriptor between probes; on saves the handshake at the cost of one idle connection per endpoint.

max_concurrent.description: MaxConcurrent bounds probes in flight per pool so that a pool with thousands of endpoints does not burst. Default 32.

timeout.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

Hedge.description: Hedge sends extra copies of a slow idempotent request to other endpoints. The first usable response wins and the others are cancelled.

delay.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

max.description: Max is the number of extra copies beyond the first, each keyed to a distinct endpoint and gated by the retry budget. Default 1; 1 to 4.

Honeypot.description: Honeypot is a decoy action: the response looks like a real page of the chosen kind, the client is logged as a security event, marked for `mark` so later requests on any route carry the label, and counted towards the `honeypot` ban reason.

body.description: Body is an inline decoy, at most 64 KiB.

body_file.description: BodyFile is a decoy read at load and reload, at most 1 MiB.

content_type.description: ContentType of body or body_file. Default text/html; charset=utf-8.

decoy.description: Decoy names a built-in body; xproxyctl honeypot lists them, and docs/CONFIG.md has the table. Exclusive with body and body_file.

delay.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

mark.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

status.description: Status of the decoy response. Default 200.

Honeytoken.description: Honeytoken is a credential that exists only to be stolen. It is planted where an attacker will find it — in a decoy this proxy serves, in a repository, in a paste, in a backup — and registered here. Nothing legitimate ever sends one, so a request that presents one is not a signal to weigh against others: it is an attacker replaying what they read, and the only question is what to do about it. The value is not a secret in the usual sense. Its whole purpose is to be read, so it is compared as an ordinary string and it is never written to a log; the logs name the token instead, which is what tells an operator which plant was found. Bodies are not searched. Every request would have to be buffered to do it, and the places a stolen credential is actually presented — the authorization header, an API key header, a cookie, a query parameter — are all in the head.

description.description: Description says where this one was planted, so the alert names the leak rather than only the token.

action.description: Action is "block" (default) or "log". Log records the hit and lets the request continue, which is what a token planted in a place legitimate traffic might also reach needs until it is proven quiet.

enabled.description: Enabled is false to keep a token configured without acting on it.

headers.description: Headers narrows the header search to these names. Empty searches every header value, which is the point for a token that might be presented anywhere.

in.description: In narrows where to look: "headers", "cookies", "query", "path". Default: all of them.

mark.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

match.description: Match is "exact" (default) or "contains". Exact compares the whole field value once the common credential prefixes ("Bearer ", "Basic ", "token ") are stripped; contains finds the token anywhere in the value, for a token planted inside a larger document a client echoes back.

name.description: Name identifies the token in the logs, the metrics and the management view. It is what an operator sees instead of the value.

status.description: Status answers a blocked request. Default 403.

values.description: Values are the planted strings. At least one of Values and ValuesFile is required.

values_file.description: ValuesFile holds one value per line (blank lines and # comments ignored), for tokens generated by something else. Re-read on reload; must not be world readable.

ICAP.description: ICAP holds scanning services (RFC 3507; AMR-015, AMR-028).

body_limit_action.description: BodyLimitAction is bypass (pass without scanning) or reject (413) for bodies above MaxBody. Default reject.

connect_timeout.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

fail.description: Fail is open (pass when the service errors or times out) or closed (answer 502). Default closed.

max_body.description: MaxBody bounds the body sent for scanning. Default 10 MiB.

max_conns.description: MaxConns bounds pooled idle connections. Default 8.

preview.description: Preview is auto (from OPTIONS), off, or a byte count.

timeout.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

url.description: URL is icap://host[:port]/service or icaps://... for TLS.

ICAPTLS.description: ICAPTLS pins the CA and name for icaps.

Ingress.description: Ingress is Kubernetes ingress controller mode: the proxy reads Ingress, Service, EndpointSlice and TLS Secret resources of one ingress class from the API server with the pod's service account, appends the resulting routes, upstreams and certificates to this configuration and reloads when they change. Routes and upstreams in this file are kept and take precedence by name.

allow_http.description: AllowHTTP permits a plain http api_server (tests, kubectl proxy).

ca_file.description: CAFile verifies the API server. Default /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/ca.crt.

cert_dir.description: CertDir receives the certificate files. Default /var/lib/xproxy/ingress.

class.description: Class is the ingressClassName served. Default xproxy.

debounce.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

listener.description: Listener names the TLS listener that receives certificates from Ingress TLS secrets. Empty ignores TLS secrets.

namespaces.description: Namespaces restricts the watch. Empty watches every namespace.

resync.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

timeout.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

token_file.description: TokenFile is the bearer token (the service account token). Default /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token.

watch.description: Watch opens watch streams on the resources so that a change syncs within debounce instead of resync. Default true.

JWTProvider.description: JWTProvider describes one issuer and where its keys come from.

algorithms.description: Algorithms allowed, from RS256, RS384, RS512, PS256, PS384, PS512, ES256, ES384, ES512, EdDSA, HS256, HS384, HS512. "none" is never allowed. Default: [RS256, ES256, EdDSA].

audiences.description: Audiences: the token's aud must contain at least one. Empty accepts any audience (not recommended).

clock_skew.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

forward_claims.description: ForwardClaims maps upstream header names to claim names. Client supplied values of these headers are always removed first.

hmac_secret_file.description: HMACSecretFile holds the shared secret for HS* algorithms.

introspection.description: Introspection validates tokens at an OAuth 2.0 token introspection endpoint (RFC 7662): opaque tokens always, signed tokens too with always. A provider may have introspection alone, without keys.

issuer.description: Issuer must equal the token's iss claim.

jwks_ca_file.description: JWKSCAFile pins the CA for the JWKS fetch. Default: system pool.

jwks_file.description: JWKSFile is a JSON Web Key Set on disk (re-read on reload).

jwks_refresh.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

jwks_url.description: JWKSURL fetches the key set over HTTPS at start and every JWKSRefresh, and on an unknown key id (rate limited).

log_claims.description: LogClaims lists claims copied into the access log (for example sub).

required_claims.description: RequiredClaims must be present. exp is always required.

source.description: Source is where the token is read from: bearer (Authorization: Bearer), header:<Name> or cookie:<Name>. Default bearer.

strip_token.description: StripToken removes the token from the forwarded request. Default true.

Journald.description: Journald is the native journald sink.

socket.description: Socket is the journald datagram socket. Default /run/systemd/journal/socket.

Limits.description: Limits are the global resource protections of the data plane. Every limit has a conservative default and can only be raised deliberately.

idle_timeout.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

max_buffered_body_bytes.description: MaxBufferedBodyBytes is the process-wide ceiling on request bodies held in memory at once by the features that materialise one (upload_guard, sensitive_data, account_guard, openapi, graphql, body_rewrite, wasm, the WAF's body inspection, a virtual patch's body pattern, a mirrored request). Default 512 MiB; 0 is unbounded. Each of those is bounded per request, and the product was the real ceiling: max_connections_per_ip times max_body_bytes is about 2.5 GiB of heap from one address at the defaults, sent slowly enough to stay inside read_timeout. A request that does not fit the budget is refused with 503 rather than buffered.

max_tarpits.description: MaxTarpits bounds requests held in a tarpit at once. A tarpitted request releases its concurrency slot first; above this bound the request is rejected at once instead of held. Default 1024.

read_header_timeout.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

read_timeout.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

write_timeout.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

Listener.description: Listener describes a single accepting socket.

dns.description: DNS configures a kind: dns listener.

forward.description: Forward configures a kind: forward listener.

h2c.description: H2C accepts HTTP/2 without TLS (prior knowledge and Upgrade) on a plaintext http listener, for gRPC clients inside a trusted network. Default false.

h3.description: H3 tunes HTTP/3 when the protocols include h3.

kind.description: Kind is http (default), tcp (an L4 listener that forwards connections by TLS server name without terminating TLS), forward (an explicit HTTP proxy for clients: CONNECT tunnels and absolute URI requests to destinations the policy allows) or dns (a DNS proxy).

protocols.description: Protocols accepted. Defaults to [h1, h2] with TLS and [h1] without.

proxy_protocol.description: ProxyProtocol enables PROXY protocol v1/v2 parsing on accepted connections. Only enable behind a trusted L4 balancer.

redirect_to_https.description: RedirectToHTTPS makes a plaintext listener answer every request with a 308 redirect to https. Useful for the :80 listener.

tcp.description: TCP configures a kind: tcp listener.

always_log.description: AlwaysLog logs a line whatever the sampling when the response is a 4xx/5xx or the request was denied. Default true. Access stream only.

fields.description: Fields, when set, keeps only these attributes on the access line (request_id, client_ip, method, host, path, status, ...); empty keeps them all. Access stream only.

format.description: Format is json (default), or for the access stream common (Common Log Format), combined (NCSA combined) or custom with Template. The other streams are structured and stay JSON.

max_size_mb.description: MaxSizeMB triggers rotation when the file exceeds this size. 0 disables internal rotation (use logrotate or journald instead).

sample_percent.description: SamplePercent logs this percentage of access lines (0 to 100, default 100). Metrics count every request regardless. Access stream only.

sinks.description: Sinks lists where the stream goes: file, journald, syslog. Default [file].

template.description: Template is the line for format custom: literal text with {field} placeholders naming access log attributes plus time_clf, time_iso, time_unix, request, user and bytes_out_clf; a missing field prints "-".

Logging.description: Logging configures the four log streams (AMR-014).

journald.description: Journald configures the journald sink used by streams listing it.

level.description: Level is the minimum level for the error log: debug, info, warn, error.

otlp.description: OTLP configures the OpenTelemetry log sink used by streams listing otlp in their sinks.

redaction.description: Redaction removes or pseudonymises personal data before any sink.

siem.description: SIEM configures the HTTPS batch sink for security information and event management systems, used by streams listing siem.

stdout.description: Stdout mirrors all streams to standard output (useful under journald and in containers).

syslog.description: Syslog configures the syslog sink used by streams listing it.

allow_cidrs.description: AllowCIDRs are always served (operators, health checkers).

allow_header.description: AllowHeader, "Name: value", exempts a request carrying it (a shared bypass token behind another gate).

enabled.description: Enabled is the state at start; the runtime toggle overrides it.

message.description: Message is the response body. Default a short text.

retry_after.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

Management.description: Management configures the control plane listener used by xproxyctl.

history_dir.description: HistoryDir keeps every applied configuration as a file for xproxyctl history, diff and rollback. Empty disables history.

history_keep.description: HistoryKeep is how many entries are kept. Default 20.

socket.description: Socket is the path of the Unix domain socket. Empty disables management.

socket_mode.description: SocketMode is the octal permission mode of the socket, default 0660.

Masque.description: Masque configures UDP proxying (RFC 9298) and IP proxying (RFC 9484) over extended CONNECT. Both need HTTP/2 or HTTP/3, so the listener needs tls with h2 in its protocols.

ip.description: IP accepts connect-ip. It also needs ip_device, ip_assign and ip_routes: a userspace process cannot put an arbitrary IP packet on the wire without a tunnel device.

ip_assign.description: IPAssign are the prefixes a client is told to use as its source address; packets from anything else are dropped.

ip_device.description: IPDevice is an existing tun interface the operator created, addressed, routed and firewalled (Linux only).

ip_routes.description: IPRoutes are the ranges a client may send to; packets to anything else are dropped.

max_sessions.description: MaxSessions bounds concurrent MASQUE sessions. Default 1024.

udp.description: UDP accepts connect-udp. The destination policy applies to each association exactly as it does to a CONNECT tunnel.

Metrics.description: Metrics configures Prometheus exposition and sampled series (AMR-026). The management socket always serves /metrics; Listen adds a TCP endpoint for scrapers.

allow_cidrs.description: AllowCIDRs restricts scrapers by source address. Empty allows any address that reaches the listener.

endpoint_series.description: EndpointSeries exposes five series per upstream endpoint. Default true; turn off above a few thousand endpoints (about 1 KiB per endpoint per scrape).

listen.description: Listen is an optional host:port serving only /metrics. Binding all interfaces requires TLS with a client CA.

otlp.description: OTLP pushes the same metrics to an OpenTelemetry collector.

per_route.description: PerRoute exposes request counters per route (one series per route and status class). Default true.

retention.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

sample_interval.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

tls.description: TLS makes the listener HTTPS; ClientCAFile requires client certificates.

MetricsTLS.description: MetricsTLS is the metrics listener certificate and optional client CA.

MirrorDiff.description: MirrorDiff configures the comparison of a shadow response with the live response. Status is always compared; headers are compared for the listed names; bodies are compared by length and digest up to MaxBodyBytes. The outcome is counted in xproxy_mirror_diff_total and a sampled share of the differing exchanges is logged.

headers.description: Headers are the response header names compared between the two responses. Empty compares no headers (status and body only).

max_body_bytes.description: MaxBodyBytes bounds the bytes of each response digested for the body comparison. Default 64 KiB.

sample_percent.description: SamplePercent is the share of shadowed requests whose difference is logged (metrics count every one). Default 100.

Normalization.description: Normalization decides what the proxy does with encoding tricks in the request target before anything else looks at it. Routing already decodes and cleans the path; these checks refuse the forms that make two components disagree about what a request means, and optionally fold Unicode spellings for routing.

reject_ambiguous_framing.description: RejectAmbiguousFraming refuses HTTP/1 requests whose framing is ambiguous: both Transfer-Encoding and Content-Length, several differing Content-Length values, or a transfer coding other than chunked. The Go parser already refuses most of these; the check closes the rest and counts them. Default true.

reject_backslashes.description: RejectBackslashes refuses a backslash anywhere in the decoded path. IIS, Apache on Windows and .NET read it as a separator while this proxy reads it as an ordinary character, so "/static\\..\\admin" is one opaque segment under /static here and "/admin" there: the route's access lists, filters, WAF profile and rate limits are all skipped for a resource the origin serves. Default true.

reject_control_chars.description: RejectControlChars refuses a decoded path or query containing a control character (below 0x20, or 0x7f), NUL included. Default true.

reject_dot_segments.description: RejectDotSegments refuses a "." or ".." segment in the decoded path (including the "..;" form servlet containers resolve). Routing resolves dot segments while the upstream receives the path as sent, so "/static/../admin" would be routed as "/admin" but reach the origin unchanged; browsers never send such paths. Default true.

reject_double_encoding.description: RejectDoubleEncoding refuses a path that still contains a percent escape after one decoding (%252e%252e). Default false.

reject_encoded_slashes.description: RejectEncodedSlashes refuses %2F and %5C in the raw path: the routing decoder turns them into separators that the upstream may treat as data. Default false.

reject_invalid_utf8.description: RejectInvalidUTF8 refuses a decoded path that is not valid UTF-8 (overlong and truncated sequences). Default true.

reject_path_params.description: RejectPathParams refuses a ";" in the decoded path. Tomcat, Jetty, JBoss and Spring strip a path parameter from every segment before mapping, so "/admin;x" or "/admin;jsessionid=..." misses this proxy's /admin route and its policy while the origin serves /admin. Default true.

unicode.description: Unicode is off, nfc or nfkc: the decoded path is normalised to that form for routing (the upstream receives the original), so composed and decomposed spellings, and with nfkc compatibility forms such as fullwidth letters, match the same route. Default off.

OCSPStapling.description: OCSPStapling configures the background OCSP fetcher of a listener.

refresh.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

timeout.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

OTLP.description: OTLP is the OpenTelemetry push exporter: every interval the metric families are sent as OTLP/HTTP with JSON encoding to a collector (counters as cumulative monotonic sums, gauges, histograms as cumulative explicit bucket histograms).

allow_http.description: AllowHTTP permits a plain http endpoint.

ca_file.description: CAFile pins the collector's CA. Default: system pool.

compress.description: Compress gzips the request body. Default true.

endpoint.description: Endpoint is the collector's metrics URL, for example https://otel.example.com:4318/v1/metrics.

headers.description: Headers added to every request (for example Authorization).

interval.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

service_name.description: ServiceName is the service.name resource attribute. Default xproxy.

timeout.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

OTLPExport.description: OTLPExport is a collector endpoint for traces or logs.

allow_http.description: AllowHTTP permits a plain http endpoint.

batch.description: Batch is the largest number of items per push. Default 512.

ca_file.description: CAFile pins the collector's CA. Default: system pool.

compress.description: Compress gzips the request body. Default true.

endpoint.description: Endpoint is the collector URL (/v1/traces or /v1/logs).

interval.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

queue.description: Queue bounds items waiting for a push. Default 8192.

service_name.description: ServiceName is the service.name resource attribute. Default xproxy.

timeout.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

OriginSignature.description: OriginSignature is the bypass protection an origin verifies: an HMAC over method, host, path, query, time, client address, request id and the listed extra headers, carried in one header.

body_digest.description: BodyDigest makes the signature cover the request body of methods that carry one, as a SHA-256 the proxy also sends in Content-Digest. Default false. Without it a signature proves that a request passed through the proxy, not what it carried: anything that can reach the origin can replay a captured header set with a body of its own while the timestamp is inside the TTL. It costs buffering the body, and a bodied request larger than 8 MiB is refused rather than forwarded with a signature that stops at the headers.

header.description: Header carries the signature. Default X-Xproxy-Signature.

include.description: Include lists extra request headers covered by the signature.

secret_file.description: SecretFile is the keyring shared with the origin (created when missing; rotate with xproxyctl rotate-secret, the previous key stays valid for verification).

ttl.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

OutlierEjection.description: OutlierEjection configures passive health checking: consecutive failures and, when latency_threshold or latency_factor is set, an endpoint whose smoothed time to first byte is slow.

base_ejection_time.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

latency_factor.description: LatencyFactor ejects an endpoint whose smoothed latency exceeds the pool's smoothed latency times this factor (at least 1.5), when the pool has two or more endpoints. 0 disables.

latency_min_samples.description: LatencyMinSamples is how many responses an endpoint must have answered since it last became available before its latency is judged. Default 20.

latency_threshold.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

pattern.description: Pattern is an RE2 expression matched anywhere in the body.

content_types.description: ContentTypes narrows the inspection to these media types (type/* allowed). Empty inspects every body.

max_bytes.description: MaxBytes bounds the body inspected. Default 64 KiB.

over_limit.description: OverLimit decides a body larger than MaxBytes, or one the filter could not read: "match" (default) treats it as matching the patch, "skip" lets it through unmatched. A virtual patch is the emergency control that holds a known vulnerability while the application is fixed, and every sibling control here refuses an oversize body rather than passing it. With "skip", 64 KiB of padding carries the same payload straight to the origin.

PatchMatch.description: PatchMatch is one condition on a named parameter, header or cookie.

pattern.description: Pattern is an RE2 expression matched anywhere in a value; empty means presence suffices.

QueryParamPolicy.description: QueryParamPolicy describes one allowed query parameter.

type.description: Type is string (default), int, number, bool, uuid or enum (with Values).

pattern.description: Pattern is an RE2 expression every value must match in full.

required.description: Required refuses requests without the parameter.

max_length.description: MaxLength bounds each value; 0 means no bound.

max_repeat.description: MaxRepeat bounds how many times the parameter may appear. Default 1.

values.description: Values are the allowed values for type enum.

RateLimit.description: RateLimit is a named rate limit policy referenced by routes: a token bucket (rate and burst) or a sliding window (limit per window).

action.description: Action is reject (429) or tarpit. Default reject.

algorithm.description: Algorithm is token_bucket (default; rate and burst) or sliding_window (limit and window).

distributed.description: Distributed selects the cluster semantics: approximate (default; each node refills at the rate minus its peers' reported consumption) or exact (one node owns each key, chosen by rendezvous hashing over the connected members, and decides for the others; a node that cannot reach the owner within cluster.exact_timeout decides locally). Needs the cluster section.

key.description: Key selects the bucket identity: client_ip, client_net, route, country, endpoint, ja4, header:<name>, cookie:<name> or jwt:<claim>. Keys that a request may lack fall back to the client address.

limit.description: Limit is the number of requests allowed per Window (sliding_window).

net_v4.description: NetV4 and NetV6 are the prefix lengths for key client_net. Default 24 and 48.

tarpit_delay.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

window.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

Redaction.description: Redaction rules. Presence enables them; Enabled false switches them off without removing the configuration.

claims.description: Claims is keep, hash or drop and applies to jwt_* attributes and client_cn. Default hash.

client_ip.description: ClientIP is keep, truncate (IPv4 /24, IPv6 /48) or hash (keyed HMAC-SHA256, stable per installation). Default truncate.

drop_fields.description: DropFields lists further attribute names removed from log lines.

hash_secret_file.description: HashSecretFile holds the key for hash mode; created on first use.

referer.description: Referer is keep, origin (scheme and host only) or drop. Default origin.

streams.description: Streams the rules apply to. Default [access, security, error]; the audit stream keeps full detail unless listed.

user_agent.description: UserAgent is keep or drop. Default keep.

Redirect.description: Redirect is a static redirect action. To may use the request variables (${path}, ${raw_query}, ${host}, ${1}...) to build the target.

Respond.description: Respond is a static response action.

RetryBudget.description: RetryBudget limits the rate of retries relative to live requests. A retry (or a hedged copy) is only sent while the number of retries in flight to the pool stays below Percent of the requests in flight, with MinConcurrency always allowed so a low-traffic pool can still retry.

min_concurrency.description: MinConcurrency is the number of concurrent retries always allowed regardless of Percent, so a pool with little live traffic can still retry. Default 3; 1 to 10000.

percent.description: Percent caps retries in flight at this share of requests in flight. Default 20; 1 to 1000.

RewriteRegex.description: RewriteRegex is a regular expression path rewrite. Replace may use ${1} to ${9} and ${name} for the pattern's groups, and the request variables of header templates (docs/CONFIG.md, "Variables").

Route.description: Route maps a request to an upstream and attaches policies.

allow_cidrs.description: AllowCIDRs / DenyCIDRs implement simple IP access control. Deny is evaluated first. Empty allow means allow all.

cache.description: Cache stores responses of this route (needs the cache section).

challenge.description: Challenge gates unverified clients with the browser challenge.

compress.description: Compress overrides the compression section for this route: false turns it off, true requires the section.

compress_authenticated.description: CompressAuthenticated overrides compression.compress_authenticated for this route.

cors.description: CORS answers cross-origin requests for this route: it short-circuits preflight OPTIONS and adds the response headers to actual requests.

deceive.description: Deceive answers a client this route no longer trusts with a plausible response instead of the origin's.

doh.description: DoH answers DNS over HTTPS on this route through a dns listener.

error_pages.description: ErrorPages overrides the server's error pages for this route.

filters.description: Filters names entries of the top-level filters list, run in the listed order within their stage.

geo.description: Geo allows or denies by client country (needs the geoip section).

grpc.description: GRPC restricts the route to gRPC requests, optionally to listed services or methods.

headers.description: Headers and Cookies are conditions on the request: every listed match must hold. Entries with conditions rank above entries without at the same path length (more conditions first).

honeypot.description: Honeypot serves a decoy and marks the client instead of proxying.

host_header.description: HostHeader overrides the Host header sent upstream. Default keeps the client Host.

hosts.description: Hosts are exact host names or wildcard patterns ("*.example.com"). Empty matches any host.

icap.description: ICAP hands requests and/or responses to a scanning service.

jwt.description: JWT requires or accepts a validated token from a provider.

maintenance.description: Maintenance overrides the global maintenance gate for this route: false always serves it (health, status), true always holds it.

max_body_bytes.description: MaxBodyBytes overrides the global body limit for this route (may only lower it unless allow_raise is set).

mirror.description: Mirror copies requests of this route to a second upstream.

path_regex.description: PathRegex lists RE2 patterns that must match the whole cleaned path (anchored at both ends by the proxy). A regex entry ranks by the length of its literal prefix; at equal length it beats a prefix entry. With PathRegex set, Paths has no default.

paths.description: Paths are prefixes. "/" matches everything. Longest prefix wins.

policy.description: Policy is the route's positive security model: what a request may look like; everything else is refused before any other processing.

priority.description: Priority breaks ties between routes with identical specificity. Higher wins. Default 0.

priority_class.description: PriorityClass is low, normal, high or critical (never shed). Default normal.

redirect.description: Redirect answers with a redirect instead of proxying.

respond.description: Respond answers with a static status instead of proxying.

rewrite_regex.description: RewriteRegex rewrites the outbound path with a regular expression and capture groups; exclusive with rewrite_path, applied after strip_prefix. A path that does not match is sent unchanged.

static.description: Static serves files from a directory instead of proxying.

tenant.description: Tenant is a free label that groups routes for quota reporting (GET /v1/quotas, xproxyctl quotas) and the per route metrics.

timeout.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

waf.description: WAF overrides the global WAF mode and profile for this route.

websocket.description: WebSocket allows Upgrade: websocket to be forwarded. Default false.

websocket_guard.description: WebSocketGuard inspects the frames of an upgraded connection. Without it an upgrade is an opaque tunnel.

webtransport.description: WebTransport relays WebTransport sessions (extended CONNECT over HTTP/3 on a listener with h3) to the upstream, which must speak HTTP/3 (h3: true): bidirectional and unidirectional streams and datagrams in both directions. Default false.

when.description: When is a condition in the expression language (docs/CONFIG.md, "Expressions") that must hold in addition to the matches above; it counts as one condition for specificity.

RouteCORS.description: RouteCORS is a Cross-Origin Resource Sharing policy for a route. It is independent of the gRPC-web preflight handling (grpc.web_origins).

allow_credentials.description: AllowCredentials sets Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true and echoes the specific origin (never "*").

allow_headers.description: AllowHeaders are the request headers a preflight may allow; "*" reflects the requested headers. Default: reflect the request's Access-Control-Request-Headers.

allow_methods.description: AllowMethods default to GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE.

allow_origins.description: AllowOrigins are the permitted Origin values: exact ("https://a.example"), a single "*" (any origin; incompatible with allow_credentials), or a wildcard host pattern ("https://*.example.com"). Required.

max_age.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

RouteCache.description: RouteCache is a route's caching policy.

cookies.description: Cookies allows caching requests that carry a Cookie header. Default false: such requests bypass the cache.

headers.description: Headers are request headers whose values join the key (for example Accept-Encoding when the upstream does not send Vary).

ignore_cache_control.description: IgnoreCacheControl stores responses regardless of Cache-Control and applies ttl. Default false.

query.description: Query is "all" (default), "none" (ignore the query string in the key) or "listed" (only the names in query_params, sorted).

ttl.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

RouteChallenge.description: RouteChallenge selects when a route challenges unverified clients.

level.description: Level is the load level that activates load mode. Default 0.5.

mode.description: Mode is off, always or load. In load mode clients are challenged only while the shedding load level is at or above Level.

RouteDoH.description: RouteDoH is the DNS over HTTPS action (RFC 8484): GET with a base64url dns parameter or POST with an application/dns-message body, answered by the named kind: dns listener's policy and cache.

RouteGRPC.description: RouteGRPC matches gRPC requests (content type application/grpc) by the service and method in the path (/package.Service/Method). Empty lists match every gRPC request. Denials and proxy errors on such a route are answered as gRPC statuses.

services.description: Services are fully qualified service names.

web.description: Web accepts gRPC-web requests from browsers (application/grpc-web and grpc-web-text, over HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2) and translates them to gRPC for the upstream: the response trailers become a trailer frame in the body and the text variant is base64 encoded. Default false.

web_origins.description: WebOrigins answers CORS preflights of gRPC-web clients from these origins (exact, or "*") and adds the allow and expose headers to responses. Empty handles no CORS.

RouteGeo.description: RouteGeo is a country policy. Deny is evaluated first; a non-empty Allow admits only the listed countries. Unknown says what happens to an address the database does not know: allow (default) or deny.

RouteICAP.description: RouteICAP attaches a service to a route.

request.description: Request sends requests (REQMOD); Response sends responses (RESPMOD). Request defaults to true, Response to false.

RouteJWT.description: RouteJWT attaches a provider to a route.

required.description: Required rejects requests without a token with 401. Default true. When false, a missing token passes and an invalid one is rejected.

RouteMirror.description: RouteMirror sends a copy of each request (sampled by percent) to another upstream in the background. The copy carries the same path rules, host and header operations as the live request plus X-Xproxy-Mirror: 1; its response is discarded and never affects the client. Bodies are buffered up to max_body_bytes; larger requests are proxied but not mirrored.

diff.description: Diff compares the shadow response with the live one and reports the differences, turning the mirror into traffic shadowing for validating a new backend against the current one. Off when unset.

max_body_bytes.description: MaxBodyBytes bounds the buffered body. Default 1 MiB.

max_in_flight.description: MaxInFlight bounds copies in flight for this route; beyond it copies are dropped and counted. Default 64.

methods.description: Methods restricts copies to these methods. Empty copies every method except upgrades.

timeout.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

RoutePolicy.description: RoutePolicy is a positive security model for a route: allowed methods, media types and query parameters, and bounds on the URI, headers and query. A request outside the policy is refused (405, 415, 400, 414 or 431) with reason policy before rate limits, filters and the WAF run, and the refusal feeds ban triggers under policy.

content_types.description: ContentTypes allowed for requests with a body: media types or type/* patterns; others get 415. Empty allows any.

max_headers.description: MaxHeaders bounds the number of header fields; MaxHeaderBytes the sum of their names and values. 0 means no bound (the server limit still applies).

max_query_bytes.description: MaxQueryBytes bounds the raw query string; MaxQueryParams the number of parameters (repeats counted). 0 means no bound.

max_uri_length.description: MaxURILength lowers server.limits.max_uri_length for the route.

methods.description: Methods allowed; others get 405 with an Allow header. Unlike routes[].methods, which selects the route, this refuses. Empty allows any method.

query.description: Query describes the parameters; with DenyUnknown, parameters not listed are refused.

require_content_type.description: RequireContentType refuses a body without a Content-Type header.

RouteStatic.description: RouteStatic serves files from a directory. Paths are resolved inside Root with os.Root, so neither ".." nor a symbolic link can leave it.

cache_control.description: CacheControl is sent with every file. Default none.

dot_files.description: DotFiles serves names starting with a dot. Default false.

fallback.description: Fallback is a path inside Root served when the requested file does not exist (single page applications: /index.html). Default none.

index.description: Index is the file served for a directory. Default index.html; empty string disables ("" in YAML).

listing.description: Listing renders a directory without an index. Default false.

max_file_bytes.description: MaxFileBytes refuses larger files with 404. Default 0 (no bound).

root.description: Root is the absolute directory served.
